endorsements.quote: Though there are significant efficiency improvements provided by these technologies, their use should support clinical judgment and not supplant it.
In the future, the research should focus on clinical validation, designing natural human-AI interfaces, and large-scale training of healthcare providers.
Resolving this calls for explicit incorporation of diversified datasets and ongoing fairness monitoring through the model's development and clinical deployment.

unlisted_practices: Involve clinicians and nursing staff in co-designing AI tools from the outset.
Involve patients and families in the design and implementation of AI tools.
Educate clinicians in AI fundamentals and incorporate digital literacy, algorithmic critique, and collaborative human-AI decision-making into medical curricula.
Build cybersecurity into AI monitoring technologies as an inherent component.
Preserve human contact and the nurse-patient relationship when deploying AI in intensive care.
Develop an ethical framework for AI through collaboration among clinicians, developers, and ethicists.
Improve interoperability of proprietary data systems and legacy infrastructure to support AI deployment.

screen.reason: This is an editorial/perspective discussing the promises, perils, and recommendations for AI deployment, governance, and ethical implementation in critical care.
